o:
We need a mutable priority queue: priorities change between polls, and ties break toward the smaller eventId. The standard technique is a lazy heap: push a new entry on every update and discard stale entries (whose recorded priority no longer matches the live map) when polling.

Example 1: initial heap has (7,5),(7,2),(4,9); poll returns 2 (tie broken by id); updating 9 to 7 pushes (7,9); next poll pops 5; then 9. Example 2 drains the heap then returns -1.
k: Lazy deletion: keep a live priority map; heap entries whose priority differs from the map are stale and get skipped at poll time.

a.n: Approach 1: Lazy max-heap with a live priority map
a.i: Store entries (-priority, eventId) in a min-heap (simulating a max-heap) alongside a map eventId → current priority. pollHighest pops until it finds an entry matching the live map, removes it, and returns it. updatePriority overwrites the map and pushes a fresh entry. Each operation amortizes to O(log n).
s: Init: fill the map and heap from the events list.
updatePriority: set map[eventId] = newPriority; push (-newPriority, eventId).
pollHighest: pop entries while the top is stale (id absent from the map or priority mismatched); if the heap empties return -1; otherwise delete the id from the map and return it.
a.t: O(log n) amortized per operation — each pushed entry is popped at most once
a.sp: O(n) — heap may hold several stale entries per event

a.n: Approach 2: Balanced BST / ordered set of (priority, eventId)
a.i: Keep an ordered set keyed by (-priority, eventId) plus the live map. Updates erase the old key and insert the new one; polls take the first element. Deterministic O(log n) per operation without stale entries, at the cost of needing a balanced-BST structure (TreeSet in Java, std::set in C++; in Python/JS one can simulate with a sorted container or bisect on a list).
s: Init: insert (-p, eid) for each event into the ordered set and record priorities.
updatePriority: erase (-old, eid), insert (-new, eid), update the map.
pollHighest: if the set is empty return -1; otherwise erase and return the first element's id.
a.t: O(log n) per operation with a real balanced BST; the bisect/sorted-list variants are O(n) per update due to list shifting
a.sp: O(n) — one entry per active event, no staleness

w: Default to the lazy heap — it is the shortest correct solution in every language. Pitfalls: tie-breaking (encode eventId so smaller wins), forgetting to delete from the live map on poll (would resurrect stale entries), and assuming updatePriority targets inactive events (guaranteed not to happen). Follow-up: support deactivating events by id, or return the k highest-priority events.
